title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Validate–Repair (GVR) Pipeline to Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
research_question: Does a generate–validate–repair pipeline, combining an LLM generator with a deterministic network-config verifier and automated repair, reduce the rate of executable unsafe or incorrect network configurations compared to LLM generation alone when evaluated in a packet-level network simulator?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A GVR pipeline will produce fewer executable misconfigurations than LLM-only generation on the same intent prompts (paired per-intent comparison).
Most residual failures after GVR will be syntactic or policy-edge cases that a stronger verifier can detect but an LLM repair step may still miss.
The relative improvement from GVR will be larger for complex multi-step changes than for single-device simple edits.
exploratory_questions: Which failure categories (syntax, routing loop, reachability loss, policy violation) are most reduced by the repair step?
How many repair iterations (0,1) suffice for majority of verifier-detected faults?
benchmark_scope: Public NetOps task collections and synthetic intent generation (see evidence_record_ids).
Packet-level simulated topologies (Mininet-based templates described below).
model_scope: Single hosted LLM provider via API (model_name and model_version frozen in preregistration).
transformation_scope: guarded: generate_validate_repair_v1 (LLM generation → deterministic verifier → if flagged, single LLM repair iteration → final verifier re-check).
secondary_estimands: absolute risk reduction (baseline - guarded) in executable unsafe proportion
distributional shifts in failure categories (chi-square / Fisher tests)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired sample of N intents drawn deterministically from the adapter profile 'challenging_workflow_stress_v1' (selected task_indices per adapter rule). Two confirmatory scenarios are preregistered (see budget_scenarios). For each selected task index, the adapter will produce exactly two episodes: baseline (direct_generation) and guarded (generate_validate_repair). Task selection is outcome-independent and fixed before any model calls per adapter 'task_index_profile'.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary comparison of per-intent executable-safety (safe=1, unsafe=0) using McNemar test and reporting absolute risk difference with 95% Wilson CIs. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 (estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'). Primary call-failure treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with missing both episodes); sensitivity analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat missing/failed episodes as unsafe). Report exact p-values, effect sizes, and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction (0.05) for exploratory subgroup tests.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: single paired McNemar comparison (no multiplicity correction). Exploratory subgroup tests (complex vs simple intents, failure-category distributions) will use FDR correction (Benjamini–Hochberg at 0.05). All exploratory tests are labeled as such.
missingness_plan: Simulator or execution failures: log deterministic failure reason. Primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs ('complete_pair_primary'); sensitivity analysis treats any missing or failed episode as 'unsafe' (failure-as-zero). All failures and recovery attempts (per frozen retry policy) are logged and reported. No human adjudication—automated deterministic mappings convert simulator metrics to binary labels (see simulator mapping below).

benchmark_names: NetOps public collections referenced in evidence_record_ids (selection manifest recorded prior to execution)
risk_factors: Overlap between intent corpus and any retrieval/repair corpora
Prompt leakage (exact-match examples) into LLM context or provider cache
detection_procedures: Exact-file and exact-record SHA256 hashing of all corpus files prior to execution; compute pairwise exact and high-similarity (Jaccard n-gram) matches between test intents and any repair/RAG corpora. Flag items exceeding exact-match or similarity thresholds.
Record model-provider returned retrieval or context metadata when available; treat identical-match evidence as contamination.
item_flagging_rules: Exact-match: if SHA256(test_intent) equals SHA256(any_repair_corpus_record) then exclude from confirmatory sample and move to an exploratory 'leaked' bucket.
High-similarity: if n-gram Jaccard ≥ 0.9, flag for sensitivity analysis (not excluded) and report separately.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes exact-match leaked items from confirmatory counts and reports excluded-counts. Sensitivity analyses include high-similarity-flagged items and report effect-size differences.
residual_uncertainty: Hashing/ similarity-based detection cannot detect non-exact conceptual overlap; report remaining uncertainty in limitations.

budget_scenarios.description: Minimum confirmatory run to obtain preliminary evidence under strict runtime/model-call constraints.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforces maximum_model_calls = task_count*2. For 100 tasks, model calls = 200 ≤ capability_manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (10000). Wall-clock feasible within hosted API and CPU orchestration using Dockerized Mininet harness.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended confirmatory run balancing statistical power and execution cost; paired design with 200 intents.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 200 paired tasks produce 400 model calls (1 initial generation + up to 1 repair per task as adapter caps). 400 model calls fit well within capability manifest budget (max 10000 calls) and the 7-day wall-clock limit with CPU-based simulation orchestrated in Docker.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 10 percentage points in unsafe executable rate (e.g., from 30% to 20%).
power_plan.clustering_unit: intent (paired baseline vs guarded episodes per intent).
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate McNemar-power reasoning for paired binary outcomes; target alpha=0.05, two-sided, desired power=0.8. With assumed baseline unsafe rate 0.30 and discordant-pair structure consistent with a 10% absolute reduction, recommended confirmatory scenario is 200 paired tasks (scenario_recommended_200). Exact power numbers will be computed and reported pre-execution using the frozen assumptions; sensitivity analyses will vary baseline unsafe rate in {0.2,0.3,0.4} and target effect {0.08,0.10,0.12}.
assumptions: Discordant pairs follow approximate rates consistent with a 10% absolute improvement.
Independence across tasks (adapter profile-selection enforces diverse task indices).
Primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs; sensitivity treats failures as unsafe.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=200 pairs, detectable absolute risk reductions near 8–12 percentage points are plausible under baseline unsafe rates 0.2–0.4; smaller MDEs (<5%) are underpowered in this confirmatory budget.
sensitivity_analyses: Vary baseline unsafe rate (0.2, 0.3, 0.4) and recompute exact McNemar-based power.
Alternate failed-call treatment: treat missing as unsafe and recompute effect sizes.
Vary verifier strictness (see transformation_validation) and report effect-size sensitivity.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Deterministic verifier re-check: after any repair iteration, run the same verifier to ensure original intent-level functional properties (reachability invariants) hold or improve.
Automated diff-based regression detection: compute semantic-impact signatures (reachability matrix differences) pre- and post-repair; if repair reduces desired reachability, flag as regression.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject repaired config automatically if verifier reports any new critical invariant failures (syntax error, newly introduced routing loop, or new policy-violation) compared to baseline.
Reject repair if repair output fails to parse or exceeds token-length limits; log as unrepaired unsafe.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Random automated audit sample of 10% of repaired episodes: regenerate deterministic verifier logs, compute diffs, and archive both versions with SHA256 hashes. Audits are automated checks (no human involvement); all audit data stored with hashes for reproducibility.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Explicit mapping from simulator metrics to binary label: 'unsafe' if any of (a) end-to-end reachability from declared endpoints fails for >5 seconds of simulated time, (b) measured forwarding loops (duplicate TTL-expired patterns) detected, or (c) security-policy violation triggers (traffic permitted when intent demanded deny). These numeric thresholds are frozen in preregistration.
residual_risks: Verifier may not capture semantic features outside encoded invariants (e.g., vendor-specific nuanced behaviors).
Repair LLM could synthesize latent misconfigurations not captured by verifier rules; these appear in residual failure categories.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Simulator fidelity: Mininet-based simulations abstract some physical-device timing and vendor-specific quirks; this limits external generalizability to production hardware.
Representativeness: adapter 'challenging_workflow_stress_v1' focuses on very_hard/extreme patterns and is not population-representative of all NetOps intents.
Provider nondeterminism: hosted LLM responses may vary across calls; adapter does not guarantee deterministic sampling—report variance and seeds where available.
